August 24, 2026

To: Appeals Department  
[Payer or Medicaid managed-care organization name]  
[Appeals mailing address, fax number, or online submission information]

Re: Appeal of denial of partial knee replacement  
Member: Skyler Kimura  
Member ID: W957444780  
Procedure: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446  
Reference number: POC-76F81E7C00-72674  
Date of denial notice: August 24, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The denial states that the imaging submitted did not support medical necessity. I respectfully request that the decision be reversed and that authorization be granted.

The submitted MRI from July 24, 2026 demonstrates advanced structural disease in the affected knee. It shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease. These findings directly document severe loss of the joint cartilage and are consistent with the patient’s persistent pain, restricted motion, and functional impairment.

The clinical record also demonstrates that symptoms have continued despite substantial conservative treatment:

- Progressive knee pain has been present for 24 months and has not been relieved by rest.
- The patient completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 26, 2026, through July 21, 2026. Therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, and the physical-therapy discharge note documents completion.
- NSAIDs were used for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026 provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- The patient cannot climb stairs without assistance and wakes three to four times each night because of pain.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

The record therefore contains both objective imaging evidence of severe medial-compartment disease and documented failure of nonoperative treatment. The imaging findings should be reviewed together with the patient’s symptoms, examination, functional limitations, and treatment history rather than considered in isolation.

The patient also has no documented active infection or untreated substance use, has a BMI of 29, and is a nonsmoker. The requested procedure is being recommended by Duval, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, based on the complete clinical picture.

I request a full reconsideration by a qualified orthopedic physician who was not involved in the initial denial. If the denial is upheld, please provide the specific imaging requirement or other clinical criterion that was applied, identify the exact medical policy or clinical-review document and version used, and explain precisely why the July 24, 2026 MRI does not satisfy that criterion. The exact payer-specific medical policy and clinical-review criteria were not included in the notice available to me, and I have not quoted a policy because that document was not publicly identified or retrieved.

Please also provide the complete clinical-review record, including the reviewer’s qualifications, the records considered, and any additional information needed for reconsideration. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the decision in writing.

This appeal must be received by February 20, 2027, according to the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Skyler Kimura  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address, if applicable]

Enclosures:

- MRI report dated July 24, 2026
- Physical-therapy discharge note
- Physical-therapy treatment records documenting 20 completed visits
- Medication and treatment history
- Corticosteroid injection record dated May 14, 2026
- Orthopedic examination and recommendation from Duval, MD
- Copy of the adverse benefit determination notice
